# Clerk

Search these docs: `https://clerk.com/docs/search.md?q=<query>` (optional `&sdk=<sdk>`). Append `.md` to a docs page URL for markdown (the API references are OpenAPI specs instead).

## Docs

- [Clerk templates and examples](https://clerk.com/docs/templates.md): Browse Clerk-maintained quickstarts, starter templates, demos, and example applications.
- [Clerk CLI](https://clerk.com/docs/cli.md): Learn how to use the Clerk CLI to set up authentication, manage configuration, and integrate with AI agents.

- [Maintenance Mode](https://clerk.com/docs/maintenance-mode.md): Learn about Clerk's Maintenance Mode.
- [Pin a Clerk SDK](https://clerk.com/docs/pinning.md): Learn how to pin a Clerk SDK to a specific version.
- [Core concepts](https://clerk.com/docs/getting-started/core-concepts.md): Learn about the main concepts and objects that drive Clerk's powerful authentication and user management system.

- [The Backend `OrganizationMembership` object](https://clerk.com/docs/reference/backend/types/backend-organization-membership.md): The Backend OrganizationMembership object is the model around an Organization membership entity and describes the relationship between users and Organizations.
- [The Backend `OrganizationSettings` object](https://clerk.com/docs/reference/backend/types/backend-organization-settings.md): The Backend OrganizationSettings object holds information about the Organization-related settings of the current instance.
- [The Backend `Organization` object](https://clerk.com/docs/reference/backend/types/backend-organization.md): The Backend Organization object holds information about an Organization, as well as methods for managing it. However, the it is different from the Organization object in that it is used in the Backend API and is not directly accessible from the Frontend API.
- [The Backend `PhoneNumber` object](https://clerk.com/docs/reference/backend/types/backend-phone-number.md): The Backend PhoneNumber object describes a phone number.
- [The Backend `RedirectUrl` object](https://clerk.com/docs/reference/backend/types/backend-redirect-url.md): The Backend RedirectUrl object represents a redirect URL in your application. This object is used in the Backend API.
- [The Backend `SamlConnectionIdpCertificate` object](https://clerk.com/docs/reference/backend/types/backend-saml-connection-idp-certificate.md): The Backend SamlConnectionIdpCertificate object represents an Identity Provider (IdP) signing certificate trusted by a SAML connection.
- [Auth object](https://clerk.com/docs/reference/backend/types/auth-object.md): The Auth object contains information about the current user's session.
- [The Backend `SamlConnection` object](https://clerk.com/docs/reference/backend/types/backend-saml-connection.md): The Backend SamlConnection object holds information about a SAML connection for an Organization.
- [The Backend `AgentTask` object](https://clerk.com/docs/reference/backend/types/backend-agent-task.md): The Backend AgentTask object represents an Agent Task.
- [The Backend `SessionActivity` object](https://clerk.com/docs/reference/backend/types/backend-session-activity.md): The Backend SessionActivity object models the activity of a user session, capturing details such as the device type, browser information, and geographical location.
- [The Backend `AllowlistIdentifier` object](https://clerk.com/docs/reference/backend/types/backend-allowlist-identifier.md): The Backend AllowlistIdentifier object holds information about a AllowlistIdentifier of your application. However, the Backend AllowlistIdentifier object is different from the AllowlistIdentifier object in that it is used in the Backend API.
- [The Backend `Session` object](https://clerk.com/docs/reference/backend/types/backend-session.md): The Backend Session object holds information about a Session of your application. However, the Backend Session object is different from the Session object in that it is used in the Backend API.
- [The Backend `APIKey` object](https://clerk.com/docs/reference/backend/types/backend-api-key.md): The Backend APIKey object holds information about an API key of your application.
- [The Backend `SignInToken` object](https://clerk.com/docs/reference/backend/types/backend-sign-in-token.md): The Backend SignInToken object holds information about a sign-in token.
- [The Backend `Client` object](https://clerk.com/docs/reference/backend/types/backend-client.md): The Backend Client object holds information about the authenticated sessions in the current device. However, the Backend Client object is different from the Client object in that it is used in the Backend API.
- [The Backend `TestingToken` object](https://clerk.com/docs/reference/backend/types/backend-testing-token.md): The Backend TestingToken object holds information about a Testing Token.
- [The Backend `EmailAddress` object](https://clerk.com/docs/reference/backend/types/backend-email-address.md): The Backend EmailAddress object is a model around an email address.
- [The Backend `User` object](https://clerk.com/docs/reference/backend/types/backend-user.md): The Backend User object holds information about a user of your application. However, the Backend User object is different from the User object in that it is used in the Backend API.

Clerk protects your users against brute force attacks by locking out accounts with too many sign-in attempts until a set period of time has passed.

- [CSRF protection](https://clerk.com/docs/guides/secure/best-practices/csrf-protection.md): CSRF is an attack that tricks the victim into submitting a malicious request. It inherits the identity and privileges of the victim to perform an undesired function on the victim’s behalf.
- [Fixation protection](https://clerk.com/docs/guides/secure/best-practices/fixation-protection.md): Session fixation is an attack that permits an attacker to hijack a valid user session. The attack explores a limitation in the way the web application manages the session ID, more specifically the vulnerable web application. When authenticating a user, it doesn’t assign a new session ID, making it possible to use an existent session ID.

- [`<OrganizationProfile />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/components/organization/organization-profile.md): Clerk's <OrganizationProfile /> component is used to render a beautiful, full-featured Organization management UI that allows users to manage their Organization profile and security settings.

- [`<SignInButton>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/components/unstyled/sign-in-button.md): The <SignInButton> component is a button that links to the sign-in page or displays the sign-in modal.
- [`<UserProfile />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/components/user/user-profile.md): Clerk's <UserProfile /> component is used to render a beautiful, full-featured account management UI that allows users to manage their profile and security settings.
- [`<UserButton />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/components/user/user-button.md): Clerk's <UserButton /> component is used to render the familiar user button UI popularized by Google.
- [`<UserAvatar />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/components/user/user-avatar.md): Clerk's <UserAvatar /> component is used to render the familiar user avatar on its own.
- [`<UNSAFE_PortalProvider>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/components/utilities/portal-provider.md): Clerk's <UNSAFE_PortalProvider> component is used to render Clerk floating UI elements inside custom containers instead of document.body.
- [`<ClerkLoading>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/components/control/clerk-loading.md): The <ClerkLoading> renders its children while Clerk is loading, and is helpful for showing a custom loading state.
- [`<RedirectToUserProfile />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/components/control/redirect-to-user-profile.md): The <RedirectToUserProfile /> component will navigate to the user profile URL which has been configured in your application instance. The behavior will be just like a server-side (3xx) redirect, and will override the current location in the history stack.
- [`<RedirectToSignIn />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/components/control/redirect-to-sign-in.md): The <RedirectToSignIn /> component will navigate to the sign in URL which has been configured in your application instance. The behavior will be just like a server-side (3xx) redirect, and will override the current location in the history stack.

The behavior will be just like a server-side (3xx) redirect, and will override the current location in the history stack.
- [`<ClerkLoaded>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/components/control/clerk-loaded.md): The <ClerkLoaded> component guarantees that the Clerk object has loaded and will be available under window.Clerk. This allows you to wrap child components to access the Clerk object without the need to check it exists.
- [`<Show>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/components/control/show.md): The Show component protects content or even entire routes based on authentication, and optionally, authorization.
- [`<RedirectToSignUp />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/components/control/redirect-to-sign-up.md): The <RedirectToSignUp /> component will navigate to the sign up URL which has been configured in your application instance. The behavior will be just like a server-side (3xx) redirect, and will override the current location in the history stack.

- [`<ClerkDegraded>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/components/control/clerk-degraded.md): The <ClerkDegraded> component indicates that Clerk is partially operational.
- [`<RedirectToTasks />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/components/control/redirect-to-tasks.md): The <RedirectToTasks /> component will navigate to the tasks flow which has been configured in your application instance when users have pending session tasks. The behavior will be just like a server-side (3xx) redirect, and will override the current location in the history stack.
- [`<AuthenticateWithRedirectCallback />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/components/control/authenticate-with-redirect-callback.md): Clerk's <AuthenticateWithRedirectCallback /> component is used to implement custom OAuth flows. It handles the OAuth callback and completes the authentication process.

The behavior will be just like a server-side (3xx) redirect, and will override the current location in the history stack.

The device can be a browser, a native application or any other medium that is usually the requesting part in a request/response architecture.

- [`BillingPaymentTotals`](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/types/billing-payment-totals.md): The BillingPaymentTotals type represents the cost breakdown for a payment.
- [`SessionVerification`](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/types/session-verification.md): The SessionVerification interface represents the state of a session reverification process.
- [`BillingProrationDiscount`](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/types/billing-proration-discount.md): The BillingProrationDiscount type represents a prorated discount applied during a billing cycle.
- [`BillingPaymentResource`](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/types/billing-payment-resource.md): The BillingPaymentResource type represents a payment attempt for a user or Organization.
- [`BillingSubscriptionNextPayment`](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/types/billing-subscription-next-payment.md): The BillingSubscriptionNextPayment type represents the upcoming payment for a subscription.
- [`SignInInitialValues`](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/types/sign-in-initial-values.md): The type for the initialValues prop that is used to pre-populate the sign-in form.
- [`ImageResource`](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/types/image-resource.md): The ImageResource type represents an image resource.
- [`SignInRedirectOptions`](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/types/sign-in-redirect-options.md): An interface that provides options for sign-in redirect methods.
- [`HandleOAuthCallbackParams`](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/types/handle-o-auth-callback-params.md): A type representing the parameters for an OAuth-related callback.
- [clerkMiddleware()](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/clerk-middleware.md): The clerkMiddleware() helper integrates Clerk authentication into your Next.js application through Middleware.
- [`@clerk/eslint-plugin`](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/eslint-plugin.md): Learn how to use Clerk's ESLint plugin to find unprotected Next.js resources.
- [Clerk Next.js SDK](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/overview.md): The Clerk Next.js SDK gives you access to prebuilt components, React hooks, and helpers to make user authentication easier.
- [`getAuth()`](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/pages-router/get-auth.md): The getAuth() helper retrieves authentication state from the request object.
- [`buildClerkProps`](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/pages-router/build-clerk-props.md): Clerk uses buildClerkProps to inform the client-side helpers of the authentication state of the user. This function is used SSR in the getServerSideProps function of your Next.js application.
- [Server Actions](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/app-router/server-actions.md): Learn how to use Clerk with Server Actions.
- [`currentUser()`](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/app-router/current-user.md): Use the currentUser() helper to access information about your user inside of your Server Components, Route Handlers, and Server Actions.
- [`auth()`](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/app-router/auth.md): Access minimal authentication data for managing sessions and data fetching.
- [Route Handlers](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/app-router/route-handlers.md): Learn how to use Clerk with your Route Handlers.
- [Clerk: `<SignedOut>` is not available in @clerk/nextjs Core 3](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/errors/signedout-is-not-available-in-clerk-nextjs.md): Learn why SignedOut was removed from @clerk/nextjs in Core 3 and how to replace it with the Show component.
- [Clerk: auth() was called but Clerk can't detect usage of clerkMiddleware()](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/errors/auth-was-called.md): Learn how to handle auth() was called but Clerk can't detect usage of clerkMiddleware() when getting 404 errors in Next.js.
- [Clerk: `<Protect>` is not available in @clerk/nextjs Core 3](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/errors/protect-is-not-available-in-clerk-nextjs.md): Learn why Protect was removed from @clerk/nextjs in Core 3 and how to replace it with the Show component.
- [Clerk: `<SignedIn>` is not available in @clerk/nextjs Core 3](https://clerk.com/docs/nextjs/reference/errors/signedin-is-not-available-in-clerk-nextjs.md): Learn why SignedIn was removed from @clerk/nextjs in Core 3 and how to replace it with the Show component.

- [`Session` object](https://clerk.com/docs/react/reference/objects/session.md): The Session object is an abstraction over an HTTP session. It models the period of information exchange between a user and the server.
- [Key Clerk objects](https://clerk.com/docs/react/reference/objects/overview.md): Learn about the key objects that power Clerk's SDKs, like the Clerk, User, and Session objects.
- [`Organization` object](https://clerk.com/docs/react/reference/objects/organization.md): The Organization object holds information about an Organization, as well as methods for managing it.
- [`User` object](https://clerk.com/docs/react/reference/objects/user.md): The User object holds all the information for a user of your application and provides a set of methods to manage their account. Users have a unique authentication identifier which might be their email address, phone number or a username.
- [`Client` object](https://clerk.com/docs/react/reference/objects/client.md): The Client object keeps track of the authenticated sessions in the current device. The device can be a browser, a native application or any other medium that is usually the requesting part in a request/response architecture.
- [`SignUp` object](https://clerk.com/docs/react/reference/objects/sign-up.md): The SignUp object holds the state of the current sign-up and provides helper methods to navigate and complete the sign-up flow.
- [`Clerk` class](https://clerk.com/docs/react/reference/objects/clerk.md): The Clerk object contains a number of methods and properties for interacting with the Clerk API.
- [`SignUpFuture` object](https://clerk.com/docs/react/reference/objects/sign-up-future.md): The SignUpFuture object holds the state of the current sign-up and provides helper methods to navigate and complete the sign-up flow.
- [`SignIn` object](https://clerk.com/docs/react/reference/objects/sign-in.md): The SignIn object holds all the state of the current sign in and provides helper methods to navigate and complete the sign in process.
- [`SignInFuture` object](https://clerk.com/docs/react/reference/objects/sign-in-future.md): The SignInFuture object holds the state of the current sign-in and provides helper methods to navigate and complete the sign-in process.
- [`Billing` object](https://clerk.com/docs/react/reference/objects/billing.md): The Billing object provides methods for managing billing for a user or Organization.
- [`APIKeys` object](https://clerk.com/docs/react/reference/objects/api-keys.md): The APIKeys object provides methods for creating, listing, and revoking API keys that allow users to grant third-party services programmatic access to your application's API endpoints.
- [`<ClerkProvider>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/react/reference/components/clerk-provider.md): The <ClerkProvider> component provides session and user context to Clerk's hooks and components.
- [`<APIKeys />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/react/reference/components/api-keys.md): Clerk's <APIKeys /> component renders a UI to manage API keys.
- [Component Reference](https://clerk.com/docs/react/reference/components/overview.md): A list of Clerk's comprehensive suite of components designed to seamlessly integrate authentication and multi-tenancy into your application.
- [`<TaskChooseOrganization />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/react/reference/components/authentication/task-choose-organization.md): Clerk's <TaskSelectComponent /> component renders a UI for resolving the choose-organization task.

- [`<RedirectToUserProfile />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/react/reference/components/control/redirect-to-user-profile.md): The <RedirectToUserProfile /> component will navigate to the user profile URL which has been configured in your application instance. The behavior will be just like a server-side (3xx) redirect, and will override the current location in the history stack.
- [`<RedirectToTasks />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/react/reference/components/control/redirect-to-tasks.md): The <RedirectToTasks /> component will navigate to the tasks flow which has been configured in your application instance when users have pending session tasks. - [`<ClerkLoaded>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/react/reference/components/control/clerk-loaded.md): The <ClerkLoaded> component guarantees that the Clerk object has loaded and will be available under window.Clerk. This allows you to wrap child components to access the Clerk object without the need to check it exists.

It contains most of the information that the Session object stores, adding extra information about the current session's latest activity.

- [`Clerk` class](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/objects/clerk.md): The Clerk object contains a number of methods and properties for interacting with the Clerk API.
- [`Billing` object](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/objects/billing.md): The Billing object provides methods for managing billing for a user or Organization.
- [`Client` object](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/objects/client.md): The Client object keeps track of the authenticated sessions in the current device. The device can be a browser, a native application or any other medium that is usually the requesting part in a request/response architecture.
- [`User` object](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/objects/user.md): The User object holds all the information for a user of your application and provides a set of methods to manage their account. Users have a unique authentication identifier which might be their email address, phone number or a username.
- [`Organization` object](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/objects/organization.md): The Organization object holds information about an Organization, as well as methods for managing it.
- [`SignUpFuture` object](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/objects/sign-up-future.md): The SignUpFuture object holds the state of the current sign-up and provides helper methods to navigate and complete the sign-up flow.
- [`SignIn` object](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/objects/sign-in.md): The SignIn object holds all the state of the current sign in and provides helper methods to navigate and complete the sign in process.
- [`SignUp` object](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/objects/sign-up.md): The SignUp object holds the state of the current sign-up and provides helper methods to navigate and complete the sign-up flow.
- [`SignInFuture` object](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/objects/sign-in-future.md): The SignInFuture object holds the state of the current sign-in and provides helper methods to navigate and complete the sign-in process.
- [`Session` object](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/objects/session.md): The Session object is an abstraction over an HTTP session. It models the period of information exchange between a user and the server.
- [`APIKeys` object](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/objects/api-keys.md): The APIKeys object provides methods for creating, listing, and revoking API keys that allow users to grant third-party services programmatic access to your application's API endpoints.
- [Key Clerk objects](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/objects/overview.md): Learn about the key objects that power Clerk's SDKs, like the Clerk, User, and Session objects.
- [`<APIKeys />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/components/api-keys.md): Clerk's <APIKeys /> component renders a UI to manage API keys.
- [Component Reference](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/components/overview.md): A list of Clerk's comprehensive suite of components designed to seamlessly integrate authentication and multi-tenancy into your application.
- [`<PricingTable />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/components/billing/pricing-table.md): Clerk's <PricingTable /> component displays a table of Plans and Features that users can subscribe to.
- [`<ClerkLoaded>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/components/control/clerk-loaded.md): The <ClerkLoaded> component guarantees that the Clerk object has loaded and will be available under window.Clerk. This allows you to wrap child components to access the Clerk object without the need to check it exists.
- [`<AuthenticateWithRedirectCallback />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/components/control/authenticate-with-redirect-callback.md): Clerk's <AuthenticateWithRedirectCallback /> component is used to implement custom OAuth flows. It handles the OAuth callback and completes the authentication process.
- [`<GoogleOneTap />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/components/authentication/google-one-tap.md): Clerk's <GoogleOneTap /> component renders a UI for authenticating users with Google's One Tap API.
- [`<TaskResetPassword />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/components/authentication/task-reset-password.md): Clerk's <TaskResetPassword /> component renders a UI for resolving the reset-password task.
- [`<TaskChooseOrganization />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/components/authentication/task-choose-organization.md): Clerk's <TaskSelectComponent /> component renders a UI for resolving the choose-organization task.
- [`<SignUp />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/components/authentication/sign-up.md): Clerk's <SignUp /> component renders a UI for signing up users.
- [`<SignIn />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/components/authentication/sign-in.md): Clerk's <SignIn /> component renders a UI for signing in users.
- [`<OAuthConsent />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/components/authentication/oauth-consent.md): Clerk's <OAuthConsent /> component renders an OAuth consent screen for authenticated users.
- [`<Waitlist />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/components/authentication/waitlist.md): The <Waitlist /> component renders a waitlist form that allows users to join for early access to your application.
- [`<TaskSetupMFA />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/components/authentication/task-setup-mfa.md): Clerk's <TaskSetupMFA /> component renders a UI for resolving the setup-mfa task.
- [`<OrganizationSwitcher />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/components/organization/organization-switcher.md): Clerk's <OrganizationSwitcher /> component is used to enable the ability to switch between available Organizations the user may be part of in your application.
- [`<OrganizationProfile />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/components/organization/organization-profile.md): Clerk's <OrganizationProfile /> component is used to render a beautiful, full-featured Organization management UI that allows users to manage their Organization profile and security settings.
- [`<OrganizationList />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/components/organization/organization-list.md): Clerk's <OrganizationList /> component is used to display Organization related memberships, invitations, and suggestions for the user.
- [`<CreateOrganization />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/components/organization/create-organization.md): Clerk's <CreateOrganization /> component is used to render an Organization creation UI that allows users to create brand new Organizations within your application.
- [`<UserProfile />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/components/user/user-profile.md): Clerk's <UserProfile /> component is used to render a beautiful, full-featured account management UI that allows users to manage their profile and security settings.
- [`<UserAvatar />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/components/user/user-avatar.md): Clerk's <UserAvatar /> component is used to render the familiar user avatar on its own.
- [`<UserButton />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/js-frontend/reference/components/user/user-button.md): Clerk's <UserButton /> component is used to render the familiar user button UI popularized by Google.

### Chrome Extension

- [Chrome Extension Quickstart (Plasmo)](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/getting-started/quickstart.md): Add authentication and user management to your Chrome Extension with Clerk using Plasmo.

- [`SignUpFuture` object](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/objects/sign-up-future.md): The SignUpFuture object holds the state of the current sign-up and provides helper methods to navigate and complete the sign-up flow.
- [`Clerk` class](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/objects/clerk.md): The Clerk object contains a number of methods and properties for interacting with the Clerk API.
- [`SignIn` object](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/objects/sign-in.md): The SignIn object holds all the state of the current sign in and provides helper methods to navigate and complete the sign in process.
- [`Session` object](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/objects/session.md): The Session object is an abstraction over an HTTP session. It models the period of information exchange between a user and the server.
- [Key Clerk objects](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/objects/overview.md): Learn about the key objects that power Clerk's SDKs, like the Clerk, User, and Session objects.
- [`Billing` object](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/objects/billing.md): The Billing object provides methods for managing billing for a user or Organization.
- [`Organization` object](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/objects/organization.md): The Organization object holds information about an Organization, as well as methods for managing it.
- [`APIKeys` object](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/objects/api-keys.md): The APIKeys object provides methods for creating, listing, and revoking API keys that allow users to grant third-party services programmatic access to your application's API endpoints.
- [`SignInFuture` object](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/objects/sign-in-future.md): The SignInFuture object holds the state of the current sign-in and provides helper methods to navigate and complete the sign-in process.
- [`SignUp` object](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/objects/sign-up.md): The SignUp object holds the state of the current sign-up and provides helper methods to navigate and complete the sign-up flow.
- [`User` object](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/objects/user.md): The User object holds all the information for a user of your application and provides a set of methods to manage their account. Users have a unique authentication identifier which might be their email address, phone number or a username.
- [`Client` object](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/objects/client.md): The Client object keeps track of the authenticated sessions in the current device. The device can be a browser, a native application or any other medium that is usually the requesting part in a request/response architecture.
- [`useOrganization()`](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/hooks/use-organization.md): Access and manage the currently active Organization in your React application with Clerk's useOrganization() hook.
- [`useReverification()`](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/hooks/use-reverification.md): Clerk's useReverification() hook enhances a fetcher function to handle a session's reverification flow.
- [`useSignIn()`](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/hooks/use-sign-in.md): Access and manage the current user's sign-in state in your React application with Clerk's useSignIn() hook.
- [`useSignUp()`](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/hooks/use-sign-up.md): Access and manage the current user's sign-up state in your React application with Clerk's useSignUp() hook.
- [`useSessionList()`](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/hooks/use-session-list.md): Access and manage the current user's session list in your React application with Clerk's useSessionList() hook.
- [`useWaitlist()`](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/hooks/use-waitlist.md): Access and manage the waitlist state in your React application with Clerk's useWaitlist() hook.

- [`useOrganizationList()`](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/hooks/use-organization-list.md): Access and manage the current user's Organization list in your React application with Clerk's useOrganizationList() hook.
- [`useUser()`](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/hooks/use-user.md): Access and manage the current user's data in your React application with Clerk's useUser() hook.
- [`useOrganizationCreationDefaults()`](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/hooks/use-organization-creation-defaults.md): Retrieve Organization creation defaults for the current user in your React application with Clerk's useOrganizationCreationDefaults() hook.
- [`useSession()`](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/hooks/use-session.md): Access and manage the current user's session in your React application with Clerk's useSession() hook.
- [`useAuth()`](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/hooks/use-auth.md): Access and manage authentication state in your application with Clerk's useAuth() hook.

- [`useSignUp()`](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/hooks/legacy/use-sign-up.md): Access and manage the current user's sign-up state in your React application with Clerk's useSignUp() hook.

- [`<ClerkProvider>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/components/clerk-provider.md): The <ClerkProvider> component provides session and user context to Clerk's hooks and components.
- [Component Reference](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/components/overview.md): A list of Clerk's comprehensive suite of components designed to seamlessly integrate authentication and multi-tenancy into your application.
- [`<PricingTable />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/components/billing/pricing-table.md): Clerk's <PricingTable /> component displays a table of Plans and Features that users can subscribe to.
- [`<SignUp />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/components/authentication/sign-up.md): Clerk's <SignUp /> component renders a UI for signing up users.
- [`<Waitlist />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/components/authentication/waitlist.md): The <Waitlist /> component renders a waitlist form that allows users to join for early access to your application.
- [`<SignIn />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/components/authentication/sign-in.md): Clerk's <SignIn /> component renders a UI for signing in users.
- [`<ClerkLoaded>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/components/control/clerk-loaded.md): The <ClerkLoaded> component guarantees that the Clerk object has loaded and will be available under window.Clerk. This allows you to wrap child components to access the Clerk object without the need to check it exists.
- [`<RedirectToSignUp />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/components/control/redirect-to-sign-up.md): The <RedirectToSignUp /> component will navigate to the sign up URL which has been configured in your application instance. The behavior will be just like a server-side (3xx) redirect, and will override the current location in the history stack.
- [`<RedirectToTasks />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/components/control/redirect-to-tasks.md): The <RedirectToTasks /> component will navigate to the tasks flow which has been configured in your application instance when users have pending session tasks. The behavior will be just like a server-side (3xx) redirect, and will override the current location in the history stack.
- [`<RedirectToSignIn />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/components/control/redirect-to-sign-in.md): The <RedirectToSignIn /> component will navigate to the sign in URL which has been configured in your application instance. The behavior will be just like a server-side (3xx) redirect, and will override the current location in the history stack.
- [`<ClerkLoading>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/components/control/clerk-loading.md): The <ClerkLoading> renders its children while Clerk is loading, and is helpful for showing a custom loading state.
- [`<Show>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/components/control/show.md): The Show component protects content or even entire routes based on authentication, and optionally, authorization.
- [`<ClerkFailed>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/components/control/clerk-failed.md): The <ClerkFailed> component indicates that the Clerk object has failed to load.
- [`<AuthenticateWithRedirectCallback />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/components/control/authenticate-with-redirect-callback.md): Clerk's <AuthenticateWithRedirectCallback /> component is used to implement custom OAuth flows. It handles the OAuth callback and completes the authentication process.
- [`<ClerkDegraded>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/components/control/clerk-degraded.md): The <ClerkDegraded> component indicates that Clerk is partially operational.
- [`<UserAvatar />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/components/user/user-avatar.md): Clerk's <UserAvatar /> component is used to render the familiar user avatar on its own.
- [`<UserButton />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/components/user/user-button.md): Clerk's <UserButton /> component is used to render the familiar user button UI popularized by Google.
- [`<UserProfile />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/components/user/user-profile.md): Clerk's <UserProfile /> component is used to render a beautiful, full-featured account management UI that allows users to manage their profile and security settings.
- [`<SignInButton>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/components/unstyled/sign-in-button.md): The <SignInButton> component is a button that links to the sign-in page or displays the sign-in modal.

- [`<OrganizationSwitcher />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/chrome-extension/reference/components/organization/organization-switcher.md): Clerk's <OrganizationSwitcher /> component is used to enable the ability to switch between available Organizations the user may be part of in your application.

### Electron

- [Electron Quickstart](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/getting-started/quickstart.md): Add authentication and user management to your Electron app with Clerk.
- [Social connections (OAuth)](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/guides/configure/auth-strategies/social-connections/overview.md): Learn how to effortlessly add social connections to your application using popular social providers like Google, Facebook, GitHub and more.
- [Build a custom waitlist page](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/guides/secure/waitlist.md): Learn how to build a custom waitlist page for your application.
- [Authorization checks](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/guides/secure/authorization-checks.md): Learn how to verify and validate user Roles and Permissions within Clerk to maintain secure access control.
- [Error handling](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/guides/development/custom-flows/error-handling.md): Provide your users with useful information about the errors being returned from sign-up and sign-in requests.
- [Build a custom flow for handling user impersonation](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/guides/development/custom-flows/account-updates/user-impersonation.md): Learn how to build a custom flow using the Clerk API that handles user impersonation.
- [Handle sign-up challenges in your custom flow](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/guides/development/custom-flows/authentication/bot-sign-up-protection.md): Learn how to ensure your custom sign-up flow works with Challenge suspicious sign-ups.
- [Build a custom waitlist form](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/guides/development/custom-flows/authentication/waitlist.md): Learn how to use the Clerk API to build a custom waitlist form using Clerk's useWaitlist() hook.
- [Themes](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/guides/customizing-clerk/appearance-prop/themes.md): Clerk currently offers six prebuilt themes for you to customize the overall appearance of your Clerk app.
- [`captcha` prop](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/guides/customizing-clerk/appearance-prop/captcha.md): Utilize Clerk's captcha prop in order to change the appearance of the CAPTCHA widget.
- [Bring your own CSS](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/guides/customizing-clerk/appearance-prop/bring-your-own-css.md): Learn how to bring your own CSS to Clerk's prebuilt components.
- [`Variables` prop](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/guides/customizing-clerk/appearance-prop/variables.md): Utilize Clerk's variables property in order to adjust the general styles of the component's base theme, like colors, backgrounds, typography.
- [`Appearance` prop](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/guides/customizing-clerk/appearance-prop/overview.md): Utilize Clerk's appearance property in order to share styles across every component or individually to any of the Clerk components.
- [`Options` prop](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/guides/customizing-clerk/appearance-prop/options.md): Utilize Clerk's options prop in order to change the layout and behavior of Clerk's prebuilt components, as well as set important links to your support, terms, and privacy pages.
- [Add custom items and links to the `<UserButton />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/guides/customizing-clerk/adding-items/user-button.md): Learn how to add custom items and include external links within the <UserButton /> menu.
- [Add custom pages and links to the `<UserProfile />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/guides/customizing-clerk/adding-items/user-profile.md): Learn how to add custom pages and include external links within the navigation sidenav of the <UserProfile /> component.
- [Add custom pages and links to the `<OrganizationProfile />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/guides/customizing-clerk/adding-items/organization-profile.md): Learn how to add custom pages and include external links within the navigation sidenav of the <OrganizationProfile /> component.
- [Key Clerk objects](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/objects/overview.md): Learn about the key objects that power Clerk's SDKs, like the Clerk, User, and Session objects.
- [`SignIn` object](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/objects/sign-in.md): The SignIn object holds all the state of the current sign in and provides helper methods to navigate and complete the sign in process.
- [`Client` object](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/objects/client.md): The Client object keeps track of the authenticated sessions in the current device. The device can be a browser, a native application or any other medium that is usually the requesting part in a request/response architecture.
- [`User` object](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/objects/user.md): The User object holds all the information for a user of your application and provides a set of methods to manage their account. Users have a unique authentication identifier which might be their email address, phone number or a username.
- [`SignUp` object](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/objects/sign-up.md): The SignUp object holds the state of the current sign-up and provides helper methods to navigate and complete the sign-up flow.
- [`APIKeys` object](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/objects/api-keys.md): The APIKeys object provides methods for creating, listing, and revoking API keys that allow users to grant third-party services programmatic access to your application's API endpoints.
- [`Clerk` class](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/objects/clerk.md): The Clerk object contains a number of methods and properties for interacting with the Clerk API.
- [`SignInFuture` object](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/objects/sign-in-future.md): The SignInFuture object holds the state of the current sign-in and provides helper methods to navigate and complete the sign-in process.
- [`SignUpFuture` object](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/objects/sign-up-future.md): The SignUpFuture object holds the state of the current sign-up and provides helper methods to navigate and complete the sign-up flow.
- [`Session` object](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/objects/session.md): The Session object is an abstraction over an HTTP session. It models the period of information exchange between a user and the server.
- [`Organization` object](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/objects/organization.md): The Organization object holds information about an Organization, as well as methods for managing it.
- [`<APIKeys />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/api-keys.md): Clerk's <APIKeys /> component renders a UI to manage API keys.
- [`<ClerkProvider>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/clerk-provider.md): The <ClerkProvider> component provides session and user context to Clerk's hooks and components.
- [Component Reference](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/overview.md): A list of Clerk's comprehensive suite of components designed to seamlessly integrate authentication and multi-tenancy into your application.
- [`<TaskResetPassword />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/authentication/task-reset-password.md): Clerk's <TaskResetPassword /> component renders a UI for resolving the reset-password task.
- [`<SignUp />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/authentication/sign-up.md): Clerk's <SignUp /> component renders a UI for signing up users.
- [`<TaskChooseOrganization />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/authentication/task-choose-organization.md): Clerk's <TaskSelectComponent /> component renders a UI for resolving the choose-organization task.
- [`<SignIn />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/authentication/sign-in.md): Clerk's <SignIn /> component renders a UI for signing in users.
- [`<Waitlist />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/authentication/waitlist.md): The <Waitlist /> component renders a waitlist form that allows users to join for early access to your application.
- [`<TaskSetupMFA />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/authentication/task-setup-mfa.md): Clerk's <TaskSetupMFA /> component renders a UI for resolving the setup-mfa task.
- [`<InviteMembersButton />`](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/organization/invite-members-button.md): Clerk's <InviteMembersButton /> component is used to render a button that opens a modal for inviting new members to an Organization.
- [`<CreateOrganization />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/organization/create-organization.md): Clerk's <CreateOrganization /> component is used to render an Organization creation UI that allows users to create brand new Organizations within your application.
- [`<OrganizationSwitcher />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/organization/organization-switcher.md): Clerk's <OrganizationSwitcher /> component is used to enable the ability to switch between available Organizations the user may be part of in your application.
- [`<OrganizationList />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/organization/organization-list.md): Clerk's <OrganizationList /> component is used to display Organization related memberships, invitations, and suggestions for the user.
- [`<OrganizationProfile />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/organization/organization-profile.md): Clerk's <OrganizationProfile /> component is used to render a beautiful, full-featured Organization management UI that allows users to manage their Organization profile and security settings.
- [`<UNSAFE_PortalProvider>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/utilities/portal-provider.md): Clerk's <UNSAFE_PortalProvider> component is used to render Clerk floating UI elements inside custom containers instead of document.body.
- [`<RedirectToUserProfile />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/control/redirect-to-user-profile.md): The <RedirectToUserProfile /> component will navigate to the user profile URL which has been configured in your application instance. The behavior will be just like a server-side (3xx) redirect, and will override the current location in the history stack.
- [`<Show>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/control/show.md): The Show component protects content or even entire routes based on authentication, and optionally, authorization.
- [`<ClerkLoaded>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/control/clerk-loaded.md): The <ClerkLoaded> component guarantees that the Clerk object has loaded and will be available under window.Clerk. This allows you to wrap child components to access the Clerk object without the need to check it exists.
- [`<RedirectToOrganizationProfile />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/control/redirect-to-organization-profile.md): The <RedirectToOrganizationProfile /> component will navigate to the Organization profile URL which has been configured in your application instance. The behavior will be just like a server-side (3xx) redirect, and will override the current location in the history stack.
- [`<RedirectToSignIn />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/control/redirect-to-sign-in.md): The <RedirectToSignIn /> component will navigate to the sign in URL which has been configured in your application instance. The behavior will be just like a server-side (3xx) redirect, and will override the current location in the history stack.
- [`<RedirectToSignUp />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/control/redirect-to-sign-up.md): The <RedirectToSignUp /> component will navigate to the sign up URL which has been configured in your application instance. The behavior will be just like a server-side (3xx) redirect, and will override the current location in the history stack.
- [`<RedirectToTasks />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/control/redirect-to-tasks.md): The <RedirectToTasks /> component will navigate to the tasks flow which has been configured in your application instance when users have pending session tasks. The behavior will be just like a server-side (3xx) redirect, and will override the current location in the history stack.
- [`<RedirectToCreateOrganization />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/control/redirect-to-create-organization.md): The <RedirectToCreateOrganization /> component will navigate to the create Organization flow which has been configured in your application instance. The behavior will be just like a server-side (3xx) redirect, and will override the current location in the history stack.
- [`<ClerkFailed>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/control/clerk-failed.md): The <ClerkFailed> component indicates that the Clerk object has failed to load.
- [`<ClerkLoading>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/control/clerk-loading.md): The <ClerkLoading> renders its children while Clerk is loading, and is helpful for showing a custom loading state.
- [`<ClerkDegraded>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/control/clerk-degraded.md): The <ClerkDegraded> component indicates that Clerk is partially operational.
- [`<UserAvatar />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/user/user-avatar.md): Clerk's <UserAvatar /> component is used to render the familiar user avatar on its own.
- [`<UserButton />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/user/user-button.md): Clerk's <UserButton /> component is used to render the familiar user button UI popularized by Google.
- [`<UserProfile />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/user/user-profile.md): Clerk's <UserProfile /> component is used to render a beautiful, full-featured account management UI that allows users to manage their profile and security settings.
- [`<SignUpButton>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/unstyled/sign-up-button.md): The <SignUpButton> component is a button that links to the sign-up page or displays the sign-up modal.
- [`<SignInButton>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/unstyled/sign-in-button.md): The <SignInButton> component is a button that links to the sign-in page or displays the sign-in modal.
- [`<SignOutButton>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/components/unstyled/sign-out-button.md): The <SignOutButton> component is a button that signs a user out.

- [`EnterpriseAccount`](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/types/enterprise-account.md): An interface that represents an enterprise account.
- [`FeatureResource`](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/types/feature-resource.md): The FeatureResource type represents a Feature of a Subscription Plan.
- [`ExternalAccount`](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/types/external-account.md): The ExternalAccount object is a model around an identification obtained by an external provider (e.g., a social provider such as Google).
- [`Errors`](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/types/errors.md): An interface that represents the errors that occurred during the last API request, for use in custom flows.
- [`SignInRedirectOptions`](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/types/sign-in-redirect-options.md): An interface that provides options for sign-in redirect methods.
- [`SignInSecondFactor`](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/types/sign-in-second-factor.md): The SignInSecondFactor type represents the second factor verification strategy that can be used in the sign-in process.
- [`SignUpInitialValues`](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/types/sign-up-initial-values.md): The type for the initialValues prop that is used to pre-populate the sign-up form.
- [`SessionStatus`](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/types/session-status.md): The SessionStatus enum is used to indicate the status of a session.
- [`SignInInitialValues`](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/types/sign-in-initial-values.md): The type for the initialValues prop that is used to pre-populate the sign-in form.
- [`SignedInSessionResource`](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/types/signed-in-session-resource.md): A session for a logged-in user that is either fully active or waiting to complete additional verification steps.
- [`OAuthApplication`](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/types/oauth-application.md): The OAuthApplication object provides helpers for building custom OAuth consent flows in Clerk.

- [`SessionWithActivities`](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/types/session-with-activities.md): The SessionWithActivities object is a modified Session object. It contains most of the information that the Session object stores, adding extra information about the current session's latest activity.

- [`Waitlist`](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/types/waitlist.md): The Waitlist object holds the state of a waitlist entry and provides methods to join the waitlist.
- [`OrganizationCustomRoleKey`](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/types/organization-custom-role-key.md): A type that represents the user's Role in an Organization.

- [`PhoneNumber`](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/types/phone-number.md): The PhoneNumber object describes a phone number. Phone numbers can be used as a proof of identification for users, or simply as a means of contacting users.

- [`createClerkBridge()`](https://clerk.com/docs/electron/reference/create-clerk-bridge.md): createClerkBridge() sets up Clerk in the Electron main process, owning IPC handlers, token persistence, and OAuth deep-link transport.

- [`Options` prop](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/guides/customizing-clerk/appearance-prop/options.md): Utilize Clerk's options prop in order to change the layout and behavior of Clerk's prebuilt components, as well as set important links to your support, terms, and privacy pages.
- [Themes](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/guides/customizing-clerk/appearance-prop/themes.md): Clerk currently offers six prebuilt themes for you to customize the overall appearance of your Clerk app.
- [`Variables` prop](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/guides/customizing-clerk/appearance-prop/variables.md): Utilize Clerk's variables property in order to adjust the general styles of the component's base theme, like colors, backgrounds, typography.
- [Bring your own CSS](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/guides/customizing-clerk/appearance-prop/bring-your-own-css.md): Learn how to bring your own CSS to Clerk's prebuilt components.
- [`captcha` prop](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/guides/customizing-clerk/appearance-prop/captcha.md): Utilize Clerk's captcha prop in order to change the appearance of the CAPTCHA widget.
- [`Appearance` prop](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/guides/customizing-clerk/appearance-prop/overview.md): Utilize Clerk's appearance property in order to share styles across every component or individually to any of the Clerk components.
- [Component Reference](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/components/overview.md): A list of Clerk's comprehensive suite of components designed to seamlessly integrate authentication and multi-tenancy into your Expo application.
- [`<ClerkProvider>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/components/clerk-provider.md): The <ClerkProvider> component provides session and user context to Clerk's hooks and components.
- [`<PricingTable />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/components/billing/pricing-table.md): Clerk's <PricingTable /> component displays a table of Plans and Features that users can subscribe to.
- [`<SignIn />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/components/authentication/sign-in.md): Clerk's <SignIn /> component renders a UI for signing in users.
- [`<SignUp />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/components/authentication/sign-up.md): Clerk's <SignUp /> component renders a UI for signing up users.
- [`<Waitlist />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/components/authentication/waitlist.md): The <Waitlist /> component renders a waitlist form that allows users to join for early access to your application.
- [`<GoogleOneTap />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/components/authentication/google-one-tap.md): Clerk's <GoogleOneTap /> component renders a UI for authenticating users with Google's One Tap API.
- [`<UNSAFE_PortalProvider>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/components/utilities/portal-provider.md): Clerk's <UNSAFE_PortalProvider> component is used to render Clerk floating UI elements inside custom containers instead of document.body.
- [`<OrganizationList />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/components/organization/organization-list.md): Clerk's <OrganizationList /> component is used to display Organization related memberships, invitations, and suggestions for the user.
- [`<CreateOrganization />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/components/organization/create-organization.md): Clerk's <CreateOrganization /> component is used to render an Organization creation UI that allows users to create brand new Organizations within your application.
- [`<OrganizationProfile />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/components/organization/organization-profile.md): Clerk's <OrganizationProfile /> component is used to render a beautiful, full-featured Organization management UI that allows users to manage their Organization profile and security settings.
- [`<OrganizationSwitcher />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/components/organization/organization-switcher.md): Clerk's <OrganizationSwitcher /> component is used to enable the ability to switch between available Organizations the user may be part of in your application.
- [`<ClerkLoaded>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/components/control/clerk-loaded.md): The <ClerkLoaded> component guarantees that the Clerk object has loaded and will be available under window.Clerk. This allows you to wrap child components to access the Clerk object without the need to check it exists.
- [`<Show>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/components/control/show.md): The Show component protects content or even entire routes based on authentication, and optionally, authorization.
- [`<ClerkLoading>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/components/control/clerk-loading.md): The <ClerkLoading> renders its children while Clerk is loading, and is helpful for showing a custom loading state.
- [`<RedirectToTasks />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/components/control/redirect-to-tasks.md): The <RedirectToTasks /> component will navigate to the tasks flow which has been configured in your application instance when users have pending session tasks. The behavior will be just like a server-side (3xx) redirect, and will override the current location in the history stack.
- [`<UserAvatar />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/components/user/user-avatar.md): Clerk's <UserAvatar /> component is used to render the familiar user avatar on its own.
- [`<UserButton />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/components/user/user-button.md): Clerk's <UserButton /> component is used to render the familiar user button UI popularized by Google.
- [`<UserProfile />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/components/user/user-profile.md): Clerk's <UserProfile /> component is used to render a beautiful, full-featured account management UI that allows users to manage their profile and security settings.
- [`<SignUpButton>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/components/unstyled/sign-up-button.md): The <SignUpButton> component is a button that links to the sign-up page or displays the sign-up modal.
- [`<SignInButton>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/components/unstyled/sign-in-button.md): The <SignInButton> component is a button that links to the sign-in page or displays the sign-in modal.
- [`<SignOutButton>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/components/unstyled/sign-out-button.md): The <SignOutButton> component is a button that signs a user out.
- [`<SignInWithMetamaskButton>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/components/unstyled/sign-in-with-metamask.md): The <SignInWithMetamaskButton> component is used to complete a one-click, cryptographically-secure sign-in flow using MetaMask.

- [`useUser()`](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/hooks/use-user.md): Access and manage the current user's data in your React application with Clerk's useUser() hook.
- [`useOrganizationCreationDefaults()`](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/hooks/use-organization-creation-defaults.md): Retrieve Organization creation defaults for the current user in your React application with Clerk's useOrganizationCreationDefaults() hook.
- [`useWaitlist()`](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/hooks/use-waitlist.md): Access and manage the waitlist state in your React application with Clerk's useWaitlist() hook.
- [`useOrganization()`](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/hooks/use-organization.md): Access and manage the currently active Organization in your React application with Clerk's useOrganization() hook.

- [`User` object](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/objects/user.md): The User object holds all the information for a user of your application and provides a set of methods to manage their account. Users have a unique authentication identifier which might be their email address, phone number or a username.
- [`SignUpFuture` object](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/objects/sign-up-future.md): The SignUpFuture object holds the state of the current sign-up and provides helper methods to navigate and complete the sign-up flow.
- [`SignUp` object](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/objects/sign-up.md): The SignUp object holds the state of the current sign-up and provides helper methods to navigate and complete the sign-up flow.
- [Key Clerk objects](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/objects/overview.md): Learn about the key objects that power Clerk's SDKs, like the Clerk, User, and Session objects.
- [`SignIn` object](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/objects/sign-in.md): The SignIn object holds all the state of the current sign in and provides helper methods to navigate and complete the sign in process.
- [`Session` object](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/objects/session.md): The Session object is an abstraction over an HTTP session. It models the period of information exchange between a user and the server.
- [`APIKeys` object](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/objects/api-keys.md): The APIKeys object provides methods for creating, listing, and revoking API keys that allow users to grant third-party services programmatic access to your application's API endpoints.
- [`SignInFuture` object](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/objects/sign-in-future.md): The SignInFuture object holds the state of the current sign-in and provides helper methods to navigate and complete the sign-in process.
- [`Billing` object](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/objects/billing.md): The Billing object provides methods for managing billing for a user or Organization.
- [`Organization` object](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/objects/organization.md): The Organization object holds information about an Organization, as well as methods for managing it.
- [`Clerk` class](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/objects/clerk.md): The Clerk object contains a number of methods and properties for interacting with the Clerk API.
- [`Client` object](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/objects/client.md): The Client object keeps track of the authenticated sessions in the current device. The device can be a browser, a native application or any other medium that is usually the requesting part in a request/response architecture.
- [`BillingDiscountRedemption`](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/types/billing-discount-redemption.md): The BillingDiscountRedemption type represents a discount applied to a subscription item.

- [`BillingPlanPrice`](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/types/billing-plan-price.md): The BillingPlanPrice type represents a specific possible price for a given Clerk Billing Plan.
- [`BillingCheckoutResource`](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/types/billing-checkout-resource.md): The BillingCheckoutResource type represents information about a checkout session.
- [`BillingSubscriptionNextPayment`](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/types/billing-subscription-next-payment.md): The BillingSubscriptionNextPayment type represents the upcoming payment for a subscription.
- [`EmailLinkError`](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/types/email-link-error.md): Custom error for email links.
- [`BillingCheckoutTotals`](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/types/billing-checkout-totals.md): The BillingCheckoutTotals type represents the total costs, taxes, and other pricing details for a checkout session.
- [Configure passkeys for Expo](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/passkeys.md): Learn how to configure passkeys for your Expo application.
- [Clerk Expo SDK](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/overview.md): The Clerk Expo SDK gives you access to prebuilt components, React hooks, and helpers to make user authentication easier.
- [`useAuthViewState()`](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/native-hooks/use-auth-view-state.md): Clerk's useAuthViewState() hook reports when a native authentication flow and Clerk-owned post-authentication steps are complete.
- [`useBiometricCredentials()`](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/native-hooks/use-biometric-credentials.md): Clerk's useBiometricCredentials() hook provides biometric credential enrollment, sign-in, and session reverification for Expo apps.
- [`useHostedAuth()`](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/native-hooks/use-hosted-auth.md): Clerk's useHostedAuth() hook opens Account Portal and activates the session created there.
- [`useLocalCredentials()`](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/native-hooks/use-local-credentials.md): Clerk's useLocalCredentials() hook enables you to store and access a user's password credentials on their device.
- [`useOAuth()`](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/native-hooks/use-oauth.md): Clerk's useOAuth() hook is used to create a new OAuth flow.
- [`useSignInWithGoogle()`](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/native-hooks/use-sign-in-with-google.md): Clerk's useSignInWithGoogle() hook provides native Sign in with Google functionality for iOS and Android devices.
- [`useSignInWithApple()`](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/native-hooks/use-sign-in-with-apple.md): Clerk's useSignInWithApple() hook provides native Sign in with Apple functionality for iOS devices.
- [`useSSO()`](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/native-hooks/use-sso.md): Clerk's useSSO() hook is used to create a new SSO flow.
- [`useUserProfileCustomPageNavigation()`](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/native-hooks/use-user-profile-custom-page-navigation.md): Clerk's useUserProfileCustomPageNavigation() hook controls navigation from custom Expo native user profile pages.
- [`<UserProfileView />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/native-components/user-profile-view.md): A native profile management component providing complete account settings for iOS and Android.
- [Theming Expo native components](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/native-components/theming.md): Customize the appearance of Clerk's native iOS and Android components with a JSON theme file.
- [`<UserButton />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/native-components/user-button.md): A native avatar button component that displays the user's profile image and opens a profile management interface.
- [Expo Native Components](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/native-components/overview.md): Pre-built native authentication and user management components for iOS and Android.
- [`<AuthView />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/expo/reference/native-components/auth-view.md): A native authentication component that provides complete sign-in and sign-up flows for iOS and Android.

- [`captcha` prop](https://clerk.com/docs/expressjs/guides/customizing-clerk/appearance-prop/captcha.md): Utilize Clerk's captcha prop in order to change the appearance of the CAPTCHA widget.

- [`requireAuth()`](https://clerk.com/docs/expressjs/reference/require-auth.md): The requireAuth() middleware protects your routes by redirecting unauthenticated users to the homepage.
- [`clerkMiddleware()`](https://clerk.com/docs/expressjs/reference/clerk-middleware.md): The clerkMiddleware() function checks the request's cookies and headers for a session JWT and if found, attaches the Auth object to the request object under the auth key.
- [Clerk Express SDK](https://clerk.com/docs/expressjs/reference/overview.md): The Clerk Express SDK provides a powerful set of tools and utilities to seamlessly integrate authentication, user management, and Organization management into your Express application.
- [`getAuth()`](https://clerk.com/docs/expressjs/reference/get-auth.md): The getAuth() helper retrieves authentication state from the request object.

- [`<RedirectToSignUp />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/react-router/reference/components/control/redirect-to-sign-up.md): The <RedirectToSignUp /> component will navigate to the sign up URL which has been configured in your application instance. The behavior will be just like a server-side (3xx) redirect, and will override the current location in the history stack.
- [`<RedirectToSignIn />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/react-router/reference/components/control/redirect-to-sign-in.md): The <RedirectToSignIn /> component will navigate to the sign in URL which has been configured in your application instance. The behavior will be just like a server-side (3xx) redirect, and will override the current location in the history stack.
- [`<RedirectToTasks />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/react-router/reference/components/control/redirect-to-tasks.md): The <RedirectToTasks /> component will navigate to the tasks flow which has been configured in your application instance when users have pending session tasks. The behavior will be just like a server-side (3xx) redirect, and will override the current location in the history stack.
- [`<RedirectToUserProfile />` component](https://clerk.com/docs/react-router/reference/components/control/redirect-to-user-profile.md): The <RedirectToUserProfile /> component will navigate to the user profile URL which has been configured in your application instance. The behavior will be just like a server-side (3xx) redirect, and will override the current location in the history stack.

The behavior will be just like a server-side (3xx) redirect, and will override the current location in the history stack.

It handles the OAuth callback and completes the authentication process.

The behavior will be just like a server-side (3xx) redirect, and will override the current location in the history stack.

- [`<ClerkLoaded>` component](https://clerk.com/docs/react-router/reference/components/control/clerk-loaded.md): The <ClerkLoaded> component guarantees that the Clerk object has loaded and will be available under window.Clerk. This allows you to wrap child components to access the Clerk object without the need to check it exists.

- [`Session` object](https://clerk.com/docs/react-router/reference/objects/session.md): The Session object is an abstraction over an HTTP session. It models the period of information exchange between a user and the server.
- [`SignInFuture` object](https://clerk.com/docs/react-router/reference/objects/sign-in-future.md): The SignInFuture object holds the state of the current sign-in and provides helper methods to navigate and complete the sign-in process.
- [`SignIn` object](https://clerk.com/docs/react-router/reference/objects/sign-in.md): The SignIn object holds all the state of the current sign in and provides helper methods to navigate and complete the sign in process.
- [`SignUpFuture` object](https://clerk.com/docs/react-router/reference/objects/sign-up-future.md): The SignUpFuture object holds the state of the current sign-up and provides helper methods to navigate and complete the sign-up flow.
- [`SignUp` object](https://clerk.com/docs/react-router/reference/objects/sign-up.md): The SignUp object holds the state of the current sign-up and provides helper methods to navigate and complete the sign-up flow.
- [`User` object](https://clerk.com/docs/react-router/reference/objects/user.md): The User object holds all the information for a user of your application and provides a set of methods to manage their account. Users have a unique authentication identifier which might be their email address, phone number or a username.
- [`Billing` object](https://clerk.com/docs/react-router/reference/objects/billing.md): The Billing object provides methods for managing billing for a user or Organization.
- [`Clerk` class](https://clerk.com/docs/react-router/reference/objects/clerk.md): The Clerk object contains a number of methods and properties for interacting with the Clerk API.

- [`Client` object](https://clerk.com/docs/react-router/reference/objects/client.md): The Client object keeps track of the authenticated sessions in the current device. The device can be a browser, a native application or any other medium that is usually the requesting part in a request/response architecture.
- [`Organization` object](https://clerk.com/docs/react-router/reference/objects/organization.md): The Organization object holds information about an Organization, as well as methods for managing it.
- [`APIKeys` object](https://clerk.com/docs/react-router/reference/objects/api-keys.md): The APIKeys object provides methods for creating, listing, and revoking API keys that allow users to grant third-party services programmatic access to your application's API endpoints.
- [`Errors`](https://clerk.com/docs/react-router/reference/types/errors.md): An interface that represents the errors that occurred during the last API request, for use in custom flows.
- [`EnterpriseAccount`](https://clerk.com/docs/react-router/reference/types/enterprise-account.md): An interface that represents an enterprise account.
